mainTopic: A son's backup vow when his father makes him a נזיר, and the rule that a son, but not a daughter, may use his father's נזירות money
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a discussion about a father who vows that his young son will be a נזיר. The גמרא rejects an earlier explanation of the son's backup vow. It replaces it with a double-sided wording: 'I'll be a נזיר because of my father, or I'll be a נזיר because of myself.' It then asks what happens if the son grows שתי שערות in the middle of the term. According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה this causes no problem, and the son simply finishes his father's term. According to רבי, the only fix is for the son to keep two terms: his own and his father's. A new משנה then teaches that a son may use the money his late father set aside for his נזירות offerings, but a daughter may not. רבי יוסי limits this to a son who was already a נזיר while his father was alive. The גמרא says the rule is a הלכה about נזיר and asks why it is needed. It answers that the rule matters when the father left only a daughter, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier suggestion fails because the son is still under his father's authority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the previous wording it had suggested for the son, because the son is still under his father's control.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is still under his father's authority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down an explanation it gave just before this passage. That earlier wording doesn't work because the son is still under his father's authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier wording was linked to whether the son was old enough to make vows. But the real question for a father's נזירות over his son is whether the son has grown שתי שערות. A son without them is still under his father's authority no matter what, so the earlier wording misses the point.

keyTerms.meaning: in his authority / under his control
of his father
he stands / he remains

phrases.english: But he still remains under his father's authority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects an explanation given just before this passage begins.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The earlier proposed wording of the son's backup vow
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that the son, lacking שתי שערות, is still under his father's authority for נזירות.

steps.title: A better wording: 'because of my father, or because of myself'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the son worded his vow to cover both cases: if he is under his father's vow, he keeps it; if not, he is a נזיר on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said: 'I will be a נזיר because of my father; I will be a נזיר because of myself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new wording for the son's vow to replace the one it just rejected. Now the son ties his vow to whether he is still under his father's authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son is saying: if my father's authority still covers me, I am a נזיר through his vow. If it doesn't, I take on נזירות myself. Either way he ends up a נזיר and can bring the proper offerings without doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: I will be
because of / for the sake of
myself

phrases.english: Rather, it means that he said: I will be a נזיר because of my father,
I will be a נזיר because of myself.
phrases.notes: In other words, 'if my father's vow doesn't cover me, I'm taking on נזירות on my own.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the wording rejected in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son's vow was tied to whether he was old enough to make vows.
steps.terutzMaskana: The son's vow was tied to whether he is under his father's authority, which depends on שתי שערות.
steps.whatToRemember: The son's double-sided vow covers him whether or not his father's נזירות applies to him.

steps.title: What if he matures in the middle of the term?
steps.stepSummary: The before and after cases are clear, but the גמרא asks what happens if the son grows שתי שערות in the middle of the נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had grown two hairs from the start, he is bound by his own נזירות. If he grew them at the end, he is bound by his father's נזירות. But if he grew them in the middle, what then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new wording with a tricky timing case: the son becomes physically mature halfway through the term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hairs came before the father's vow, the son was never under his father, so his own vow takes effect. If they came after the term ended, the father's vow fully covered him. In the middle, the father's vow may stop working partway, and the son's own vow only begins then, so neither one gives him a full term.

keyTerms.meaning: two hairs, the sign of physical maturity
from the beginning
at the end
in the middle

phrases.english: If he grew two hairs from the start —
phrases.notes: 'From the start' means before his father made the vow.

phrases.english: he is bound by his own נזירות,
and if at the end — he is bound by his father's נזירות.
But if he grew them in the middle, what then?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the wording from step 2 against a hard timing case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The double-sided wording of the son's vow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If maturity comes mid-term, the father's vow may be cut short and the son's own vow only starts partway, so neither gives a complete term.

steps.title: No problem according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the father's power lasts until the son reaches עונת נדרים, so the middle case causes no trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who said the father's power lasts until the son reaches the age of vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by showing that one opinion has no difficulty here. This also sets up the harder question about the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the father's power lasts until עונת נדרים, the age of vows, which is only a rabbinic stage. So if the son reaches that point in the middle of the term, the father's vow is not automatically cancelled, and the son simply finishes his father's term.

keyTerms.meaning: this works out well (for one view)
the age when a child's vows start to count

phrases.english: This works out well according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
who said: until he reaches the age of vows.
phrases.notes: He means the father can make his son a נזיר up until this age.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 for one opinion and prepares the challenge for the other.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, reaching עונת נדרים mid-term (a rabbinic cutoff) does not cancel the father's vow, so the son completes it.

steps.title: But according to רבי, what can be said?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי, the father's power ends when the son grows שתי שערות, so the middle case is a real problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי, who said the father's power lasts until the son grows two hairs, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses the question against the second opinion, where the middle case does cause trouble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, once the hairs appear the son is no longer under his father, so the father's vow stops right there. The son's own vow only began at that moment, so he seems to be left without one full, clean term.

keyTerms.meaning: what can be said? (a challenge formula)
until he brings / grows

phrases.english: But according to רבי, who said:
until he grows two hairs,
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 4: the question that was resolved for one opinion remains for רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the son's vow works under רבי's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי, hairs mid-term end the father's vow immediately, leaving neither vow complete.

steps.title: According to רבי, he must keep both terms
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי, the only fix is for the son to keep his own term and also his father's term.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: according to רבי there is no fix until he keeps his own term and also keeps his father's term.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that under רבי there is no shortcut: the son must keep two full terms of נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we can't be sure which vow is really binding him, the son keeps both terms one after the other. That way he definitely completes a full term under whichever vow actually applies.

keyTerms.meaning: they say (introduces an answer)
a fix / remedy
sits, here meaning 'keeps a term'

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the son just finishes his father's term. According to רבי, if he matures mid-term he must keep both his own term and his father's.

phrases.english: They say: according to רבי there is no fix
until he keeps his own term
and keeps his father's term.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge raised in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under רבי, a son who matures mid-term has no remedy except keeping both his own term and his father's term.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the difficulty and requiring a stricter remedy (keeping both terms)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי, the son's double-sided vow seemed to leave him without any complete term if he grew שתי שערות mid-term.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי, the son can only be sure of a full term by keeping his own term and also his father's term.

steps.title: A son may use his father's נזירות money, but a daughter may not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a man may bring his נזירות קרבנות with money his father set aside for his own נזירות, but a woman may not. The case: the father set aside unallocated money and died, and the son then said, 'I am a נזיר on condition that I shave with Father's money.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A man can shave using his father's נזירות, but a woman cannot shave using her father's נזירות. How does this work? A father was a נזיר. He set aside money for his offerings without saying which coins were for which offering, and then he died. His son said: 'I am a נזיר on condition that I shave using Father's money.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It gives a rule: a son may use his late father's נזירות money for his own end-of-נזירות offerings, but a daughter may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To 'shave' here means to finish your נזירות by bringing the offerings and cutting your hair. Normally, unallocated money of a נזיר who died cannot be used for anyone else's offerings. The משנה says a son is the exception, even if he only became a נזיר after his father died.

keyTerms.meaning: Shaves: finishes his נזירות by bringing the offerings and cutting his hair
The state or term of being a נזיר
Unallocated money: set aside without saying which coins pay for which offering
'I am hereby a נזיר': the words used to take on נזירות

phrases.english: MISHNAH
A man can shave on his father's naziriteship,
phrases.notes: 'On his father's naziriteship' means using the money his father set aside for his own offerings.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מְגַלַּחַת עַל נְזִירוּת אָבִיהָ.
phrases.english: but a woman does not shave on her father's naziriteship.
How so?
One whose father was a nazir,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת סְתוּמִים עַל נְזִירוּתוֹ וָמֵת,
phrases.english: and he set aside unallocated money for his naziriteship and died,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: ״הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֲגַלֵּחַ עַל מְעוֹת אַבָּא״.
phrases.english: and [the son] said: "I am hereby a nazir on condition that I shave with Father's money."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, after the earlier discussion of a father making his son a נזיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son, but not a daughter, may use his late father's unallocated נזירות money for his own offerings, even if he became a נזיר only after his father died.

steps.title: רבי יוסי limits the rule to a son who was already a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees about the case just described. In his view the money goes to communal gift offerings. A son may use his father's money only if both of them were נזירים while the father was still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: In that case the money goes to gift offerings, and this is not a son shaving on his father's נזירות. Who does shave on his father's נזירות? A son who was a נזיר at the same time as his father, and the father set aside unallocated money for his נזירות and died. That son may shave on his father's נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues with the first opinion in the משנה. He says the son's later vow does not let him use the money; only a son who was already a נזיר before his father died may use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions agree that a son can sometimes use his father's money. They disagree about timing: must the son already be a נזיר when his father dies? For רבי יוסי, if the son was not yet a נזיר, the money follows the normal rule and goes to נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal gift offerings: where a dead נזיר's unallocated money normally goes
Which one is it? Introduces the case that really fits the rule

steps.confusionAlert: This is רבי יוסי, not the רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה from the earlier steps. Also, he agrees that the son-only rule exists. He only narrows the case where it applies.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: These [coins] fall to gift offerings,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין זֶה מְגַלֵּחַ עַל נְזִירוּת אָבִיו.
phrases.english: this is not one who shaves on his father's naziriteship.
Who is the one who shaves on his father's naziriteship?
One who was a nazir together with his father,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִפְרִישׁ אָבִיו מָעוֹת סְתוּמִים לִנְזִירוּתוֹ וָמֵת —
phrases.english: and his father set aside unallocated money for his naziriteship and died —

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הוּא שֶׁמְּגַלֵּחַ עַל נְזִירוּת אָבִיו.
phrases.english: this is the one who shaves on his father's naziriteship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion in the משנה that limits the case in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son may use his father's money only if he was already a נזיר during his father's lifetime; otherwise the money goes to נדבה.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the משנה's rule that a son can use his father's money but a daughter cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks where the rule comes from. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is unusual, because offering money normally cannot pass from one person to another. So the גמרא wants to know what source supports it, and why it applies to a son and not a daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? Asks for the source or logic of a rule

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source for the rule that a son, but not a daughter, may use his father's נזירות money?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: It is a הלכה about a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the rule is a הלכה, a received tradition, given specifically about a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is a הלכה regarding a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the source: the rule is a tradition passed down from סיני, not something learned from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling it a הלכה means we cannot work it out by logic alone; it is a special tradition just for נזיר. This answer leads straight into the next question: if it is a tradition, what exactly does it add?

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a הלכה למשה מסיני, a tradition handed down from סיני

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is a halakha regarding a nazir.
phrases.notes: 'הלכה' here means a tradition going back to משה at סיני, not just 'a law.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה הִיא בְּנָזִיר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule is a הלכה למשה מסיני specific to נזיר.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that a son inherits and a daughter does not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why do we need a special הלכה? A son inherits his father and a daughter does not, so of course only the son can use the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! What is it coming to teach? That a son inherits his father and a daughter does not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the rule seems obvious without any special tradition, because of the ordinary laws of inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה already says a son inherits ahead of a daughter. If the rule just means 'the heir gets the money,' the son would get it anyway. So a special הלכה seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! A challenge that a statement teaches nothing new
What is there to say? What is it teaching?
Inherits

phrases.english: That is obvious!
What is it coming to say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵן יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אָבִיו, בַּת לָא?
phrases.english: that a son inherits his father, a daughter does not?
phrases.notes: When there is a son, he inherits and the daughter does not (במדבר 27:8).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבי יוחנן's הלכה in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that a special הלכה is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ordinary inheritance law already gives the father's property to a son and not a daughter, so the tradition seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The rule is needed when the father left only a daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the הלכה matters in a case where the father has only a daughter, so she is the heir. It begins to explain what we might otherwise have thought: that the tradition was taught about heirs in general. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he has only a daughter. You might have said that we learned this rule about heirs...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a case where inheritance law does not settle it: the daughter is the only heir. Then it starts to say what we might have mistakenly thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no son, the daughter inherits everything, so inheritance law alone would let her use the money. The הלכה teaches that even then she cannot, because the tradition is about a son specifically, not about any heir. The full explanation continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for: introduces the case where a rule really teaches something
You might have said: introduces a mistaken first assumption
We learned it as a tradition

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he has only a daughter.
You might have said:
we learned it about heirs,
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going after this. The mistaken idea is that any heir, even a daughter, could use the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אֶלָּא בַּת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing to a specific case (only a daughter as heir)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tradition might have been about heirs in general, so a daughter who is the only heir could use the money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה is needed to teach that only a son may use it, even when a daughter is the only heir.
